title: Political Incentives to Suppress Negative Information: Evidence from Chinese Listed Firms

requirements.description: The appendix's empirical tables require analysis data, but no data file or compatible author-prepared analysis-data route is supplied or specified. The package does not identify the exact input files/products, fields, identifiers, period coverage, or construction needed to reproduce the reported analyses.

issues.description: The assigned package contains only the online appendix PDF; no executable author program or run instructions are supplied.

The appendix reports a broad set of alternative and supplementary analyses but supplies no executable workflow, data description, or dependency order. It refers readers to Table 1 and Appendix A for other variable definitions, which are not included in the assigned package; required analysis inputs and their compatibility therefore remain unspecified.

evidence.description: Frozen work-item inventory lists only the online appendix PDF; no code, data description, or data files are inventoried.
Appendix Table 4A reports pooled cross-sectional estimates and defines alternative political-event indicators used for the results.
evidence.quote:
Table 4A
Influence of political events on the incentive to suppress negative financial information
Inclusion of both National Congresses and Political Promotions Event Indicators in same
estimation (Footnote 15)
The following panels present coefficients from various pooled, cross-sectional estimations of the following model:

             Ncskewi,t =  + Year + Province + 1Politicali,t + 2Post-Politicali,t + 3Logsizei,t + 4Growthi,t

           + 5Sigmai,t + 6Turnoveri,t + 7Turnoveri,t-1 + 8Betai,t + 9Returni,t + 10Returni,t-1 + 10SOEi,t + i,t

The dependent variable Ncskew is the firm’s third moment of excess daily stock returns scaled by its cubed standard
deviation times minus one. Political is an indicator variable equal to one if the firm-year relates to a specific
political event; Post-Political is an indicator variable equal to one in the year immediately following the event. In
the first set of estimations, Political is an indicator variable equal to one for the years that a National Congress of the
Chinese Communist Party was held, zero otherwise; Post-Political is an indicator variable equal to one for the year
directly following each National Congress event, zero otherwise. In the second set of estimations, Political is an
indicator variable equal to one for the year preceding and corresponding to a provincial level political promotion
event, zero otherwise; Post-Political is an indicator variable equal to one for the year directly following the
provincial-level promotion event, zero otherwise. In the last set of estimations, indicators variables for both political
events are included. All other variables are defined in Table 1 and Appendix A.

scopes.description: Complete author-documented workflow for the assigned package; the supplied online appendix reports empirical tables and sensitivity analyses, but no runnable program or analysis dataset is supplied.

actions.description: Obtain the executable author workflow and compatible analysis-input specification for the appendix analyses.
steps: Request the runnable author programs and instructions for this package variant, including each entry point, required runtime/software, stated alternative branches, and the order in which programs produce and consume intermediate files.

Request the complete author-provided input inventory and specifications: exact prepared analysis files or products, formats, field names, identifiers, historical periods, constructions, and any author-supported acquisition routes. Ask for the Table 1 and Appendix A variable definitions cited by the appendix if these form part of the author instructions.
Retain all appendix analyses and stated variants in the assessed target; do not infer code, inputs, or a data-construction workflow from the reported coefficients.
validation: After receiving the materials, trace the workflow and map all appendix outputs (Tables 4A–4I, 8A, 11A, and A–F) to their actual generating entry points, supporting stages, branches, and inputs.

Review the full dependency closure and producer-consumer order; verify fields, identifiers, and required periods against bounded metadata for each author-supplied or author-identified compatible input before any separately authorized execution.

review_notes: No analysis_only scope is supported: the assigned package has no author-prepared dataset or executable analysis entry point from which a bypass and its compatible inputs can be verified.
